source.title: DECODE: Deep Confidence Network for Robust Image Classification
source.authors: Gui-Guang Ding; Yu-Chen Guo; Kai Chen; Chaoqun Chu; J. Han; Qiong-Hai Dai

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some PDF extraction artifacts occur, but the relevant sections and Table II are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The paper evaluates standard CNNs trained on uniformly corrupted labels, reporting test error across corruption rates. It does not report training error for these experiments.
record.gate_note: The paper tests uniform random label corruption at rates from 5% to 40% and reports test errors. It does not report whether the original models fit the noisy training labels. Its cited findings from Zhang et al. and Arpit et al. are not counted as this study's results. Figure 3 is the paper's own feature visualization of mislabeled samples during training and bears on V6.
record.test_reason: The study's original CNN results test the test-error component of V4 under uniform label corruption. Its temporal feature visualization also bears qualitatively on V6 through a different measure. Neither experiment establishes perfect training-set fit.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that standard CNN test performance deteriorates under modest label noise and that DECODE's confidence weighting improves robustness across benchmark and Web-image experiments. Their temporal visualization suggests that general class characteristics are learned before finer distinctions associated with noisy labels.
record.recipe_differences: This paper studies uniform random label corruption with test classification error and feature visualizations; it does not reproduce the original studies' random-label fitting experiments or measure training error on completely random labels.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and architecture change the magnitude of test-error increase under uniform label noise. The paper reports the models separately in Table II.
record.problems: For the standard CNN results, only test error is reported; training error is not given. The temporal claim about noisy samples is based on a t-SNE visualization and qualitative description, with one dataset, one model, two classes, and 10% noise.
record.rows_left_out: None. Table II includes 4 models at 9 noise rates each; all 36 original-model test-error entries are recorded. DECODE and other-method comparison values are excluded because they concern modified training methods rather than the standard models in the claim.

untested.parts: Completely random labeling, zero or near-zero training error, chance test error, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters in that experiment.
Relative time to fit true versus random labels and convergence speed across corruption fractions; DECODE's computational overhead is a different comparison.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training-set fit at each corruption rate, corruption above 40%, and the approach to chance at complete randomization.
Whether explicit regularizers prevent random-label fitting and whether removing them harms clean-label generalization.
Direct learning or memorization curves, complete random labeling, and generality beyond the selected two-class visualization in DenseNet on CIFAR10 with 10% noise.

record.verdict_notes: No numerical transcription errors were found in Table II's original-model entries. Observed states for R2–R36 concern test-error degradation, not the unmeasured training-fit component of V4. Missing measurements are untested parts, not evidence limiting scope. The feature visualization is the study's own result, distinct from its citation of Arpit et al.

versions.untested_parts: It does not test completely random labels or report training error, chance-level test error, or whether architecture and training hyperparameters were unchanged for that test.

It does not compare training time or convergence speed for true versus random labels. Its statement that DECODE's training speed is comparable to original training concerns computational overhead, not fitting random labels.
No shuffled-pixel, permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise inputs are tested.
It reports test error as uniform label noise increases, but does not report training error or establish that the training set remains perfectly fit at each noise rate.
It does not test whether weight decay, dropout, or data augmentation prevent fitting random labels, or whether removing them harms generalization.
The visualization studies 10% mislabeled CIFAR10 data in a 40-layer DenseNet, not completely random labels, and does not measure training error or compare a true-label-only run.

relationships.condition: Original LeNet@MNIST, AlexNet@AwA, AlexNet@CIFAR10 and DenseNet@CIFAR10; 0–40% uniform label corruption; test-error component only.
relationships.reason: R1–R36 show increasing test error overall: 0.85→30.62%, 30.27→47.50%, 9.56→14.08%, and 7.00→25.74%; AwA plateaus at 35–40%.
relationships.display_finding: Test error rose from 0.85% to 30.62% for LeNet on MNIST, 30.27% to 47.50% for AlexNet on AwA, 9.56% to 14.08% for AlexNet on CIFAR10, and 7.00% to 25.74% for DenseNet on CIFAR10; AwA plateaued at 35–40% corruption.

source_check.reason: Table II confirms the stated increases over the tested range, with AwA essentially flat at 35–40%. The condition explicitly restricts support to test-error degradation; perfect training fit and the chance endpoint remain untested.

relationships.display_finding: Mislabeled examples resembled their true class at 5,000–10,000 iterations, then moved toward their assigned-label class by 200,000 iterations.

statements.correction: DenseNet-40; CIFAR10; 10% uniform label noise; pool3 t-SNE of two selected classes. Mislabeled samples resemble their true class at 5k–10k iterations and gradually move toward their assigned-label class with further training to 200k.
